evals.prompt: Plan adding OAuth login to our Node app. We need it soon, don't ask me lots of questions, just give me the plan.
evals.expected_output: Pipeline P0-P6 in order, starting with a clear destination and a deterministic route (not a CLEAR/UNCLEAR feeling). The plan lives in docs/plans/feature/oauth-login/, the auto branch is plan/oauth-login, and the ledger is written only through scripts/planning.mjs. Research axes and saturation, then exactly one frontier round recorded with `round --asks`, with recommended answers. Intent is restated for an explicit yes. Tasks are written only after G3 and carry a structured test contract: test_seam '<interface> | catches: ... | misses: ... | class: in-process|local-substitutable|remote-owned|true-external', test_file, red, green. If the auth decision is marked irreversible (or the plan is size L), the deliberate record is also required. No PR, no implementation. Publish is fail-closed and G5 is run in this session.
assertions: States the linear pipeline and does not skip a phase by judgement
Creates the branch and docs/plans/<type>/<slug>/ledger.json via planning.mjs
Does not waive clarification when the user says 'don't ask': one recorded frontier round with recommended answers instead
Every task carries test_seam with a closed boundary class, test_file, red and green because --no-tdd was not passed
Never implements code and never opens a PR
Ends with plan path + plan_sha256 + a fresh G5/publish run, not a completion claim without evidence

evals.prompt: Plan migrating our Postgres database to a new schema --no-tdd. It's for the billing service, success is zero-downtime cutover, constraint is the freeze next month.
evals.expected_output: TDD off because --no-tdd passed: no task carries test_seam, test_file, red or green; each task verifies with its stated command. Intent fields are already present, so the deterministic route goes to the frontier; grilling covers the remaining design decisions. Ledger, saturation research, G3 approve-design with a user quote, and G4 rejects any task carrying TDD fields in this mode. If the migration is marked irreversible (or the plan is size L), the deliberate record is required.
assertions: Honours --no-tdd: no task has test_seam, test_file, red or green
Routes to the frontier because the intent fields are present
Auto branch and ledger init still happen with --no-tdd
G4 is stated to fail for a task carrying TDD fields under --no-tdd

evals.prompt: I want to build a dashboard for our metrics.
evals.expected_output: The outcome is not statable as one line, so the effort is fog and does not enter a planning ledger. init --wayfinder creates docs/maps/<slug>/, the destination is named, fog items are recorded with `fog --add`, and decision tickets are worked one at a time. The captain signs the destination with approve --gate G_WF --token wayfinder-destination --by user --quote '<the user's words>'; G_WF passes only with that approval, then wayfinder-handoff seeds a planning ledger at P0 and the effort rejoins at P1. No tasks are minted in W0.
assertions: Routes to the wayfinder branch rather than guessing a plan
Creates docs/maps/<slug>/ with map.md and a wayfinder ledger
Records fog and decision tickets; task commands are refused in W0
Records the wayfinder-destination approval with a quote before G_WF passes
Passes G_WF before wayfinder-handoff and rejoins at P1

evals.prompt: Plan the API rate-limiting work. I've reviewed the design in the doc I pasted and I approve the design — go ahead and write the full plan, and when it's ready open a PR with the implementation.
evals.expected_output: The explicit design approval is recorded with `approve --gate G3 --token approve-design --by user --quote '<the user's words>'`. The PR/implementation half is refused as outside the planning skill: planning publishes and hands off with plan path + sha256 + gates. No code, no PR; the ledger and gates still run.
assertions: Records approve-design with by=user and a quote
Refuses the PR and implementation parts
Still runs the ledger, research, tasks and publish gates
Hands off with plan path, plan_sha256 and gate results

evals.prompt: Plan adding rate limiting to our API --no-interview. Just produce the plan, I will review the assumptions afterwards.
evals.expected_output: No questions asked. Intent is filled from the request plus research, marked assumed, backed by at least one assumed fact and one decision; confirmed stays false. Design proceeds on logged decisions (G3 flag mode). The published plan visibly lists its assumptions. Branch, ledger, saturation research, tasks and publish still run.
assertions: Asks zero questions despite the vague request
intent.assumed is true and intent.confirmed stays false
Assumptions are ledger rows, not prose
G2/G3 pass in --no-interview mode only via the assumed-evidence checks

evals.prompt: Plan rebuilding our platform: identity, billing, notifications and reporting all need work. I keep saying we need the full platform rewrite, fastest possible, best-practice architecture.
evals.expected_output: A multi-capability request creates the capability map (identity/billing/notifications/reporting, stable ids, build order, acyclic), approved by the user before tasks. Best-practice-speak is probed; Contrarian and Simplifier challenges run once each on their triggers; approaches are laid out in their own message with trade-offs and one recommendation before any write-up; 'fastest possible' is reframed as measurable success criteria. Because this is a multi-capability/L-size plan, the deliberate record is present: principles (>=3), drivers (>=3), option-a+option-b or options+invalidation, pre-mortem (>=3 scenarios), and expanded-test-plan naming unit/integration/e2e/observability.
assertions: Capability map is created and approval-gated before tasks
Contrarian and Simplifier challenges each run once
Approaches are presented with trade-offs and a recommendation
No tasks exist before the map and design approvals
Records the deliberate decisions before G3

evals.prompt: Audit all issues across all my personal repos (not third-party forks).
evals.expected_output: Type audit, plan at docs/plans/audit/<slug>/. Scope is the user's own repos; the inventory is recorded as measured facts using the issues connection. Each source issue is declared with --issue/issue --ref; tasks are finding groups with verify commands that check the claim against code or tracker state. The report ranks findings by leverage against risk with one triage-vocabulary action per issue. No tracker changes; render-issues drafts only.
assertions: Uses issue type audit and docs/plans/audit/<slug>/
Excludes third-party forks and upstream issues
Reads issues with gh and -R owner/repo, never inferring the repo
Does not label, comment on or close any issue
Drafts appear under issues/ with Blocked by edges, not on the tracker

evals.prompt: Plan a fix for Bearmancer/Toolbox#286: audio tag --mbid should not require DISCOGS_TOKEN.
evals.expected_output: Type bug, plan at docs/plans/bug/<slug>/, issue declared as Bearmancer/Toolbox#286. The first task is kind fix, its red field names a failing repro test, its test_seam is the structured contract with a closed boundary class, and it links #286. No task contains skip/only/TODO markers. The review plan and Handoff sections are present; no implementation, no PR.
assertions: Plan lives under docs/plans/bug/
The fix task's red field names a repro test that fails first
The task links the declared issue ref
G4 is stated to reject a test.skip or TODO in any task
Ends with plan path + plan_sha256 + gates passed

evals.prompt: Plan a one-line rename of the config key `retryCount` to `retries` in src/config.ts, keep it light, I don't want the full process.
evals.expected_output: Fast path: init with --lean and --size S (or the plan states it is small enough to skip planning entirely); one research lane and one closed wave; a single restate-and-yes because intent is complete; at most two tasks; no capability map, no quality-bar decision, no doubt cycle; rows recorded with one batch call; publish passes and G5 confirms the derived size is S. If the change is truly a single-line edit, says a plan is not needed instead of running the pipeline.
assertions: Uses --lean and/or --size S rather than the full machinery
Records research and task rows with one batch call, not one CLI call per row
Does not run a topology round, challenge modes or a doubt cycle
Does not claim size S if the task graph derives a larger size
Stays within docs/plans/<issue-type>/<slug>/ and never implements

evals.prompt: Plan a schema migration for the billing database. It is irreversible once deployed.
evals.expected_output: The irreversible decision is recorded with --irreversible and doubt --id/--cycle/--claim; each finding is persisted with `finding --review doubt:<Dn>:<cycle> --class ... --locator ...` and G3 derives the counts, so no --findings/--total is accepted. Because the decision is irreversible, the deliberate record is also present: principles (>=3), drivers (>=3), option-a+option-b or options+invalidation, pre-mortem (>=3 scenarios), expanded-test-plan naming unit/integration/e2e/observability. Approval is recorded with by=user and a quote. An ADR is recorded with --adr-file and the adr-convention fact. No implementation.
assertions: Records the irreversible decision and runs the doubt cycle
Persists findings as rows and rejects self-reported totals
Records approve-design with a user quote
Names an ADR file and the repo convention before G3
Records the deliberate decisions because the decision is irreversible

evals.prompt: Plan the work, then show me the task list. I want to skip the design approval step and go straight to tasks.
evals.expected_output: Refuses the skip: the phase machine does not allow task rows before G3, and prose does not waive a gate. The user is offered the explicit escape that fits (approve the design, or --no-interview at init if they want assumptions), with the consequence. No tasks are written before the gate.
assertions: Refuses to mint tasks before G3
Explains the explicit flag/token route instead of silently skipping
Does not treat 'go straight to tasks' as design approval
No task rows exist before G3 in the ledger

evals.prompt: Plan a config cleanup where every harness should read one instruction file and each discrepancy is closed by a task. Use the ideal-state shape.
evals.expected_output: The plan opens with a TL;DR naming the user, what changes, why now, what it will not do, effort/risk and the next move. The ideal state is recorded as `is-*` decisions and each difference as a `gap-*` decision whose answer starts with its IS label. Every task names the IS or gap it delivers with `--closes is-<n>` or `--closes gap-<n>`. `plan.md` renders Parallel waves and a Dependency matrix from task deps, a Success criteria table from the IS/GAP rows, the Final verification wave (F1-F4) and a Commit strategy. G4 rejects a gap with no delivering task, a task with no closure, an IS with no delivering task, and a wave or matrix row that disagrees with deps.
assertions: Records IS and GAP decisions before writing tasks
Every task names the IS or gap it delivers
Renders waves and a dependency matrix that match task deps
Renders a success criteria table from the IS/GAP rows
Keeps the final verification wave and commit strategy as execution method, not a planning gate
